compiled_state.title: [Jira sync]: Local tickets absent from Jira and Jira tickets absent locally -> bidirectional sync not operational
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **Model ID:** claude-sonnet-4-6
* **Plugin/Tool Versions:** dso v1.16.11
* **Active Configs:** `jira.project=DIG` (.claude/dso-config.conf); `tickets.sync.jira_project_key` not set
* **Context Scope:** main repo, branch worktree-20260505-220349 at time of filing
* **code_version:** 6a6a3643beae0472f70d09122927546889312264

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

Tickets created via `.claude/scripts/dso ticket create` should appear in Jira project DIG, and tickets created in Jira should appear in the local `.tickets-tracker/` event log. The outbound bridge (`bridge-outbound.py`) is designed to push local ticket changes to Jira; an inbound bridge (`inbound-bridge.yml`) is referenced in the workflow comments. Both directions should keep the two inventories in sync.

#### Actual Behavior

User observed: all 9 locally-open bug tickets are absent from Jira. Jira tickets do not appear in `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list`. The two ticket populations are completely disjoint with no overlap.

### 3. Action History and Workarounds

* **Steps Taken:**
  * User ran `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list --type=bug --status=open` — returned 9 bugs, none visible in Jira
  * User reported Jira tickets do not appear locally
* **Raw Results:**
  * Local list output: 9 open bugs (b38d-1781, d99c-f4d4, fcea-6e83, 1348-f163, bf9f-d7b1, 014e-0b3e, 0740-2df7, b733-486e, 9726-9e3f)
  * No error messages surfaced during any ticket operation
* **Known Workarounds:** None — tickets must be manually cross-referenced between systems

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* **Outbound bridge:** `plugins/dso/scripts/bridge-outbound.py` calls `bridge/_outbound_api.py` and `bridge/_outbound_handlers.py`, which call `acli-integration.py` for Jira operations
* **Outbound CI trigger:** `.github/workflows/outbound-bridge.yml` — runs on 30-min cron or explicit `workflow_dispatch`; push trigger was removed (per workflow comment: GitHub Actions does not detect workflow files on orphan branches)
* **Inbound bridge:** referenced in outbound workflow comments as `inbound-bridge.yml`; existence and operational status not confirmed

### 6. Logs

No error output was observed from any ticket CLI operation. Sync failures, if any, are silent from the user's perspective.

### 7. Additional Details

The outbound bridge workflow comment notes the push-to-tickets trigger was removed (bug 71fa-c068) and replaced with a 30-min cron. It is not known whether the cron is currently running successfully, whether `acli-integration.py` has valid Jira credentials in CI, or whether the inbound path exists at all. Investigation should start by checking recent outbound-bridge workflow run history.

comments.body: INVESTIGATION: Jira sync requires operational credentials in CI (JIRA_API_TOKEN, JIRA_BASE_URL) and a running outbound-bridge.yml cron. No code fix is possible without verifying credential setup and CI workflow execution. Investigation needed: check recent outbound-bridge workflow runs in GitHub Actions, verify acli-integration.py has valid Jira credentials, confirm inbound-bridge.yml exists. Bug remains open pending infrastructure investigation.
comments.author: Test

comments.body:
RE-DIAGNOSIS (2026-05-06): user clarified that ACLI is locally configured with auth and GitHub has a valid JIRA_API_TOKEN. Re-investigation confirms:

INFRASTRUCTURE INTACT:
- acli v1.3.18-stable installed locally at /opt/homebrew/bin/acli
- .github/workflows/outbound-bridge.yml: vars.JIRA_URL=https://navasage.atlassian.net, vars.JIRA_USER=joeoakhart@navapbc.com, secrets.JIRA_API_TOKEN=*** (visible as masked in CI logs)
- vars.JIRA_PROJECT=DIG
- Outbound bridge cron */30 * * * * — last 5 runs all completed:success (e.g. run 25474062482 at 2026-05-07T03:15:37Z)
- Inbound bridge cron same cadence — last 5 runs all completed:success
- Bridge bot identity configured: dso-bridge[bot] / dso-bridge@users.noreply.github.com

ACTUAL FAILURE MODE:
1. Run 25474062482 logged "INFO: Outbound bridge complete: 0 SYNC events written" then "No SYNC events to commit — skipping." So the bridge runs but has nothing to push.
2. bridge-outbound.py default mode (non-backfill) calls `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD --diff-filter=A --name-only` on the tickets branch. This only sees event files ADDED in the most recent commit. Historical tickets (the 27+ pre-bridge bugs in this session) were created before the bridge was wired up — they have never been included in any commit's diff window.
3. Backfill mode (`workflow_dispatch` with input backfill=true) scans every JSON event file under .tickets-tracker/ and is idempotent (has_existing_sync() prevents duplicate Jira issue creation). It was never run.
4. Secondary concern: vars.BRIDGE_ENV_ID is unset → bridge_env_id=""; filter_bridge_events compares each event's env_id against "" so non-empty event env_ids pass through fine. Not currently breaking outbound, but a config gap that should be set to the local .tickets-tracker/.env-id value (currently `c3d2c46e-df9e-40c4-8014-5e8c9fdf3cc1` based on a sampled ticket) so bridge-written SYNC events are reliably filtered out on subsequent passes.

REMEDIATION:
- Run `gh workflow run outbound-bridge.yml -f backfill=true` once to push historical tickets to Jira (idempotent — safe to re-run).
- Set `gh variable set BRIDGE_ENV_ID --body c3d2c46e-df9e-40c4-8014-5e8c9fdf3cc1` (or whatever the canonical env_id value is for this project) to close the env-id gap.
- After backfill, monitor next two outbound runs to confirm they pick up new tickets via the HEAD~1..HEAD window.

Note: the HEAD~1..HEAD window is also a narrow miss-window: if two consecutive commits land on tickets branch between cron ticks, the older commit's events are skipped. This is a separate latent bug — file under "outbound bridge: only most-recent commit window scanned" if it manifests post-backfill.
comments.author: Test
